transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Monroe (AE), Samir Rao (SE), Leah Kim (CSM) — ZenVera: Dr. Nia Patel, Jordan Lee, Priya Singh, Marcus Green

Summary: quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and cost breakdown. Customer asks about per-model routing, dedicated pools, and encryption key management.

[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, with Samir our solutions engineer and Leah from customer success. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Nia (Customer): Good thanks, Alex. Appreciate you fitting us in. We're excited to see the analytics piece; we've been trying to get line-of-sight on per-route costs.
[00:15] Alex: Great. Quick agenda: console overview -> per-route dashboards -> cost breakdowns -> security notes -> Q&A and next steps. Samir will jump into the demo.
[00:25] Samir (SE): Cool. I'm going to share my screen — tell me if the view's fuzzy. Starting at the Console home: you can see aggregate token usage, latency percentiles, error rates. The per-route section is where it gets interesting.
[00:40] Jordan (Customer): Quick question — can we map routes to microservices in our infra? We have a bunch of internal endpoints.
[00:45] Samir: Yep, you can tag routes, attach metadata, and filter. We also expose exportable CSVs and BigQuery sinks if you want long-term analytics.
[00:55] [01:00] Samir: Here is the per-route dashboard — each route shows QPS, median and p95 latency, token consumption, and an estimated cost column which combines model unit price and usage. The cost calc uses your pricing tier and any dedicated pool discounts.
[01:20] Marcus (Customer): That estimated cost — is that real dollars or a normalized score?
[01:25] Samir: Real dollars, based on the rate card you pick in account settings. It's an estimate — we account for batching and KV cache hits as heuristics, but we'll run a pilot to calibrate for your workload.
[01:40] Priya (Security): How do you handle KMS integration? We need customer-managed keys for inference logs.
[01:45] Samir: We support KMS/HSM integrations in Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we can do envelope encryption and offer TTL controls. I'll share the SOC2 pack and KMS integration guide after the call.
[01:58] [02:10] Alex: Also, you can set route-level policies — like prefer dedicated pools for payment-sensitive routes and fall back to hosted for overflow. That routing is policy driven.
[02:25] Nia: On the per-route view, can we break down cost by model variant? Like same route but sometimes we call 8-bit quantized vs fp16.
[02:33] Samir: Yes, we show model splits. The dashboard has a stacked bar for model variants and shows per-variant token counts and cost. Note transcription: sometimes the UI says "quant profile" which is our shorthand for quantization profile.
[02:47] [03:10] Jordan: The latency numbers — are they from the edge? We care about pogo-sticks under 200ms.
[03:15] Samir: Latency is measured at the request hop in the Redwood runtime; you can add synthetic checks from your region. For sub-200ms you usually want dedicated pools and optimized kernels. There's a quick filter to show routes by p95 latency to target slow endpoints.
[03:33] [03:45] Marcus: We're also worried about cost — can Redwood show what percent of spend is from embeddings vs completions?
[03:50] Samir: Yes, the usage page has a breakdown by workload type and by route. If you tag embedding calls you get a separate row and cost projection.
[04:05] [04:30] Priya: Compliance-wise, do you retain logs? What's retention?
[04:35] Leah (CSM): You can control retention per account; hosted default is 30 days, enterprise can extend or route logs to your storage for e-discovery. We'll include details in the SOC2 doc.
[04:48] [05:05] Nia: Can you show the cost model math quickly? Like a worked example for a route with 10M tokens/month.
[05:12] Samir: Sure. So we plug in model unit price — say $0.0006/token — multiply by tokens, subtract caching/ batching savings. In the dashboard you can click a route and open a modal with a month-to-month cost forecast and what-if slider for batching and quantization.
[05:40] [06:00] Samir: (narrating UI) Here's the route detail: average tokens/request, token distribution, top prompts, and an "optimize" panel that suggests batching and model variant changes. The suggestions show projected cost delta and expected latency impact.
[06:18] Jordan: Are those suggestions automated? Can they be enforced?
[06:22] Samir: Right now they're advisory; for Dedicated customers we can apply automatic routing policies — e.g., route 95% traffic to quantized variant during non-peak. Enforcement is part of our Dedicated policies.
[06:35] [07:00] Nia: For a pilot, we want a conservative approach: mirror traffic, run offline benchmarks, then switch 10% to Redwood. Is that something you do?
[07:07] Alex: Absolutely. Typical pilot flow: mirror traffic to Redwood Dedicated or Private, run a week of bench, validate latency and regression tests, then do a canary. Samir will own the bench.
[07:20] Samir: I'll propose a sample benchmark plan: 1) synthetic RTT/throughput runs 2) replay of a 24h sample to measure cache hit behavior 3) end-to-end regression with our evals.
[07:35] [07:50] Priya: One more security — SSO/SAML and RBAC. We need scoped roles for data scientists vs ops.
[07:56] Samir: We have SSO via SAML/OIDC, and RBAC with route-level permissions. We'll show a quick demo in the follow-up or ship a tenant with your IdP for validation.
[08:10] [08:30] Marcus: Any mention of competitors? We tried Bedrock but ran into inconsistent kernel perf; curious how library of kernels compares.
[08:36] Samir: We maintain a curated kernel/compile path per architecture, and our optimizer picks kernels based on seq length distribution. It's not perfect — sometimes perf varies by model family — but we publish benchmarks and compatibility notes.
[08:52] [09:10] Nia: Ok, this looks promising. A couple of clarifying bits: 1) If we pin a model version, do you allow safe rollbacks? 2) How are fallbacks handled if a dedicated pool is saturated?
[09:20] Samir: 1) Yes, version pinning and rollbacks are supported. 2) Fallbacks can route to compatible variants in hosted capacity; you can configure policy to prefer latency or cost.
[09:35] [09:50] Alex: Let me show the cost export — you can schedule daily exports to S3 with per-route line items and an optional breakdown by token type.
[09:58] [10:10] Jordan: That export will help finance reconcile invoices. Good.
[10:15] [10:30] Priya: Are logs encrypted at rest with our KMS?
[10:33] Samir: For Dedicated and Private yes, use your KMS/HSM. For hosted we do envelope with rotation options — we'll send the exact config.
[10:45] [11:00] Nia: About the "optimize" suggestions — do you have examples of cost drop from customers?
[11:05] Samir: Typical uplift: batching + quantization with prefix caching can reduce per-token cost 30–60% depending on workload. We'll anonymize a reference case in the follow-up.
[11:22] [12:00] (short pause)
[12:10] Marcus: If we commit to Dedicated, what are minimums?
[12:14] Alex: We have monthly reserved capacity tiers; I'll include the commit options in the pricing sheet. There's also burst capacity for spikes.
[12:25] [12:40] Priya: Liability and data residency — can we ensure logs stay in EU region for EC operations?
[12:45] Leah: Yes, for Private and for region-specific Dedicated we can provision in the EU and enforce residency. Hosted can be region-specified as well subject to capacity.
[12:58] [13:15] Nia: Great. I think next steps are: 1) pilot/benchmark plan 2) pricing and commit options 3) security docs and SSO test.
[13:25] Alex: Yep. We'll put that in writing. Samir — you'll run the pilot. Leah will handle SOC2/KMS pack. I'll send pricing.
[13:35] [13:40] Priya: One small nit — sometimes the console UI shows abbreviations and we want full labels for audit. Is that a config?
[13:46] Samir: We can toggle verbose mode in account settings; will enable for you.
[13:55] [14:10] (crosstalk) Jordan: Thanks.
[14:14] Alex: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the docs and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[14:24] Nia: Appreciate it.
[14:26] Meeting end.
